Arithmetic without the library's operand checks

Source: R/methods-eval-backlog.R
eval_add_in_place_no_check.Rd

These call the C++ functions of the same names, which skip the checks OpenFHE normally makes on its operands (same context, same key, compatible levels) and do not adjust levels or scales. They are for code that has already established those conditions; with operands that do not meet them the result is not meaningful. Use eval_add_in_place(), eval_mult() and eval_mult_no_relin() otherwise.

Usage

eval_add_in_place_no_check(ct1, ct2)

eval_mult_no_check(ct, scalar)

eval_mult_no_relin_no_check(ct1, ct2)

Arguments

ct1, ct

A Ciphertext.

ct2

A Ciphertext.

scalar

A whole number of at most 2^53, or a string of decimal digits for a larger value.

Value

eval_add_in_place_no_check() returns ct1, invisibly; the other two return a new Ciphertext.

Details

eval_add_in_place_no_check() adds ct2 into ct1. eval_mult_no_check() multiplies every element of a ciphertext by an integer scalar. eval_mult_no_relin_no_check() returns the tensor product of the elements of two ciphertexts, without relinearizing. That is their product in CKKS for two ciphertexts at the same level and scale. It is not the BFV product, which includes a scaling step this function does not perform.
